title: Together Link: evaluate open models inside a familiar coding workflow
summary: Together Link connects existing coding tools to hosted open models. Its practical value deserves a task-level trial, especially because the launch post and current beta docs disagree about how often Auto changes models.

sections.title: Keep the workflow, evaluate another model
sections.html:
Together Link connects existing coding tools to hosted open models. Its appeal for educational apps, websites and creative utilities is continuity: compare another provider while keeping a familiar repository and agent workflow. Whether it preserves every integration or delivers equally good work remains a question for testing.

Together's October 5 announcement names Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, OpenCode and Pi. Current documentation labels the connector beta and warns that commands, routing and models may change. This baseline uses primary pages inspected October 26; we have not installed it or measured sessions. Announcement; beta documentation.

sections.title: A material disagreement about routing
sections.html:
The sources disagree about Auto. The launch post says it routes once per session from the first task, preserving prompt caching. Current docs describe a hosted gateway choosing a model for each request. We cannot resolve that discrepancy from these pages. Do not assume either frequency when planning costs or caching. Launch description; routing documentation.

Docs limit optional Anthropic routing to Claude Code/Desktop sessions with an Anthropic API key, billed to that account. Codex, OpenCode, Pi and ChatGPT Desktop stay on Together models, as do Claude sessions without that key.

For comparison, pin a model with togetherlink --main zai-org/GLM-5.3 claude. The full command needs --main before the tool name; a later --model may be refused or ignored. Shortcuts put the tool name first. Record the session banner's actual model.

sections.title: Prerequisites and configuration boundaries
sections.html:
Requirements are a Together API key, an installed supported tool, and macOS/Linux with Bash and curl. Installing Bun on Linux also requires unzip. Docs specify OpenCode 2 and Pi Code 0.80.8+, with Node.js 22.19+ for Pi. The installer can add Bun and local commands. Requirements.

Together describes temporary terminal configuration but persistent desktop profiles storing the API key locally. ChatGPT Desktop uses a separate profile; Claude setup includes backups. No local proxy or daemon runs: requests go to the hosted gateway.

This is documentation, not a configuration audit. Inspect key storage, billing and applicable provider terms before adoption. Our sources do not establish universal data retention or licenses for every hosted model. Keep the ordinary launcher available for comparison and recovery.

Together says normal configuration files remain unchanged. An existing account with another AI service does not replace the Together key, and local file editing does not make inference local.

sections.title: Measure completed work, not a token counterfactual
sections.html:
Together advertises over 50 percent savings. Docs describe a comparison with what the same tokens would cost on Claude Opus. That does not establish equal attempts, tool calls, quality or human repair time. Measure accepted work rather than treating the counterfactual as guaranteed project savings. Savings claim; usage documentation.

The retrieved table lists GLM 5.3 at $1.40 per million input tokens, $0.26 cached input and $4.40 output. These are a snapshot; check togetherlink models for current rates. Count total billed inference, accepted tasks, elapsed time, retries and human repairs. Include optional Anthropic charges and image spend, which the docs track separately from tokens.

sections.title: A bounded teaching-app exercise
sections.html:
A proposed teaching-app trial adds a teacher-controlled hint level to one exercise in a disposable branch. Require keyboard navigation and prevent stored answers leaking into the student view. Give each model the same starting repository, synthetic data and acceptance checklist; review the diff and both user paths.

Set an attempt limit before testing so a cheaper model does not appear successful simply because it received more retries or hints. Start pinned, then consider Auto after several representative successes. Classify failures as requirements, reasoning, integration or runtime problems. Compare familiar and held-out tasks, keeping reviewers unaware of the provider where practical. These are evaluation proposals, not demonstrated Together Link results.

This exercise combines a small data-model change, UI copy, event handling and accessibility. A teacher or developer can inspect whether the pedagogical boundary survived. A general coding benchmark cannot answer that classroom-specific question.

sections.title: Website assets and video planning
sections.html:
Docs describe an image-generation skill for launched Claude Code, Claude Desktop and ChatGPT Desktop sessions; do not assume every supported agent has it. Generate images.

For a website pilot, specify a lesson illustration's subject, dimensions, placement, accessible description and required facts. Integrate a reviewed image into one responsive page, then check mobile legibility and educational accuracy. Preserve the asset and generation details; API success does not settle reference rights.

For video preparation, build a browser storyboard from an approved script and stills, or a caption-format converter and asset checklist. The evidence does not establish a video editor or timeline integration. Judge preparation time saved while keeping the actual edit inspectable in existing production tools.

A lesson microsite could combine the diagram concept, page implementation and surrounding explanation in one session. Evaluate the finished page and retained assets together, rather than accepting an attractive image as proof that the whole workflow succeeded.

sections.title: Operational details that can derail a trial
sections.html:
Docs say Together Link ignores project .env files: explicit key arguments take priority over saved configuration, then the environment variable. Hold these setup choices and agent versions fixed during comparisons. Configuration and troubleshooting.

Headless Claude Code can block indefinitely with open standard input; docs show closing stdin as the remedy. For automated storyboard or documentation jobs, observe completion/errors and set your own timeout. Waiting for input is not evidence of slow inference.

Check a read-only request, a reversible change and required integrations before expanding. The docs describe returning to ordinary behavior by launching the tool directly; verify recovery. Keep connector/agent versions, selected model, acceptance result and usage together so beta changes do not make comparisons uninterpretable.

The ordinary agent’s safeguards and approval boundaries still need evaluation. Changing providers does not demonstrate that every extension, skill or tool call behaves identically. Preserve enough run output to distinguish a setup failure from a model failure before deciding what to replace.

sections.title: Where it earns a place
sections.html:
Together Link merits a controlled trial for builders comparing hosted open models inside established workflows. Its beta status, routing conflict and surface-specific behavior make version records and task-level results particularly important.

Open models behind a hosted gateway are not local inference, and this research did not establish every model's deployment rights. Begin with one pinned model, one representative repository and written acceptance criteria. Expand after inspecting work and usage. Documentation supports the intended workflow; it does not establish savings or reliability for your particular tools.

useCases: Compare accepted coding changes across fixed models in an existing agent.
Build a reviewed teaching-app feature with controlled requirements.
Prepare website artwork and inspectable video-production utilities.
limitations: Beta behavior and model menus may change.
Launch post describes session routing; current docs describe request routing.
Hosted gateway, API accounts and surface-specific integrations are required.
No installation, code-quality benchmark, savings test or security audit was performed.
